title: Minimal public surface hardening
summary: This iteration converts the accepted public-surface hardening plan into executable repair-and-prune constraints. Public data no longer exposes source_effectiveness, default public interaction input drops internal/source-runtime sections, the public copy gate blocks source effectiveness wording, retired platform discovery stages are invalid policy entries, and retired platform sections remain optional during report normalization.

validation_commands: node --test tests/unit.test.js --test-name-pattern "public data|public section contract|resilience policy|platform"

lessons.lesson: Public source diagnostics need runtime and artifact gates, not just prose instructions.
lessons.evidence: Default interaction output now filters verification/source-runtime sections and public docs data omits source_effectiveness.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep public-facing source diagnostics out of default report generation unless a new reader-facing section is explicitly tested and approved.

lessons.lesson: Retired platform requirements should be optional on input and rejected as new discovery stages.
lessons.evidence: Report normalization accepts absent WeChat/Zhihu/Reddit platform fields, while resilience policy validation rejects retired platform discovery stage ids.
lessons.recommended_action: Use direct RSS, GitHub watchlist, and community hotspots as the durable public lanes; keep retired platform diagnostics internal when legacy fixtures contain them.

suggestions.issue: Future public reader sections with new rich ids can be filtered until the public allowlist is updated.
suggestions.evidence: The new filter favors the existing reader-facing rich ids and denies known source-runtime ids and prefixes.
suggestions.suggestion: Add a focused test whenever introducing a new public section richId.
suggestions.expected_benefit: Prevents accidental public reintroduction of audit/runtime blocks while still allowing deliberate reader-facing additions.

followups.action: Before the next publish, run the daily dry-run on this revision and confirm public HTML/data still contain no source audit or source_effectiveness wording.
